newsitem.title: Iran: Two strong Iran quakes kill 38, cause wide damage.
newsitem.headline: Two strong Iran quakes kill 38, cause wide damage.

text.p: Two strong earthquakes killed at least 38 people and injured 90 others in northeastern Iran on Tuesday, Iranian state television said.
It said the quakes, one registering 5.4 on the Richter scale and the other registering 6.1, had their epicentre outside Bojnurd, about 580 km (360 miles) northeast of Tehran.

In the Bojnurd area alone some 38 people were reported killed and 90 injured by the quakes which struck a wide region along the border with Turkmenistan and Iran's Caspian coast at 1:24 p.m. (0954 GMT) and 44 minutes later, it added.
Tehran radio said the tremors levelled 34 villages in the Bojnurd area and caused damage in dozens of other rural communities.
Iranian media said relief efforts were underway.
Tremors of force six can cause widespread damage and those of force five are powerful enough to cause heavy damage in a populated area.
Hong Kong's Royal Observatory recorded a measurement of 6.9 for one of the quakes.
Quakes hit Iran regularly. The worst recorded one, measuring 7.3 on the Richter scale, killed 35,000 people in a densely populated area near the Caspian coast in 1990.
